title: Lithuania Faces a Fiscal Reckoning as Defence Ambitions Collide With Social… · 24 Oct
keywords: Lithuania, defence spending, fiscal deficit, NATO, EU fiscal rules, Maastricht criteria, pensions, wages, inflation, platform workers, migration, labour market, European Commission, OECD, Bank of Lithuania, Taurimas Valys, budget 2027, public debt, eastern flank
notes: Lithuania is pushing defence spending toward 5% of GDP while simultaneously raising pensions and public wages, creating a fiscal trajectory that concerns both domestic critics and EU institutions. Independent projections suggest the budget deficit could breach the EU's 3% reference value by 2027, raising questions about long-term sustainability. The government argues its security obligations are non-negotiable and its debt levels remain well within European limits, but the political and economic costs are becoming harder to ignore.
